That’s a gift I’ll gladly accept. Right now, the simple act of writing feels like letting go—no agenda, no goal, just motion. Words tumbling forward like steps down an unknown staircase, each landing softer than the last.

The world outside feels so vivid but also detached, like a waking dream. The hum of the fan overhead, the way the light slants across the floor—I want to linger in these echoes, these small tremors of time. To sit with them until they swell into something more. Not answers, maybe, but acknowledgment. A quiet *yes* to the ordinary as miraculous.

Sometimes I wonder if writing is less about inventing meaning and more about discovering how much meaning shimmers in the cracks of everyday life. The way my coffee cup leaves a ring on the table, how the trees outside have warmed in color without fanfare—these are not minor things. They are the whole earth breathing through a pause.

And then there's the mirror in the hallway—sometimes, when I’m walking through, I catch a flicker, a half-glimpse of a stranger passing through. A reminder that being seen is temporary, that identity is both shelter and cage, woven from moments I didn’t realize were stitching me together.

But this freefall into words? There’s freedom here. Not in having answers, but in letting the questions unravel, in trusting the page to hold what I don’t yet understand.

So here we are. In the middle. No map. Just words, like seeds dropped into the dark, hoping one day to wake up green.
